 More than 720,000 BMVs recalled over fire risk 
 By 
 Angela Barbuti 
 Published 
 Nov. 14, 2026, 8:04 a.m. PT 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 More than 720,000 BMW vehicles have been recalled over fears they could catch fire — even when parked or turned off — according to an alert from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
 The fire risk stems from faulty water pumps that could short-circuit if moisture seeps through an “improperly sealed electrical connector,” according to an NHTSA safety recall report issued Nov. 4.
 “Over time, due to material degradation at the connector, this could allow moisture to enter the pump and lead to the possibility of a short circuit,” the document states. “This could increase the risk of a thermal event and, in rare cases, a fire.”
 3 
 The 2014 BMW 428i is one of the cars affected by the recall. Getty Images 
 The recall affects 14 models of the cars, manufactured by BMW of North America, based in Westwood, NJ, between 2012 and 2018:
 2014-2016 BMW 228i

 3 
 The 2013 BMW 328i is another vehicle that was recalled. Getty Images 
 There have been “approximately 10 field instances” in the country of the faulty part causing issues for drivers, but “BMW has not received any reports, nor is BMW otherwise aware, of any accidents or injuries related to this issue,” the report noted.
 The affected vehicles were previously recalled in 2024 over a water pump defect, but now require additional repairs.
 3 
 Owners of the recalled BMWs are being asked to park “outside and away from structures.” dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images 
 The company is still working on rectifying the problem, but in the meantime, owners are being advised to park outside and away from buildings. 
 “The remedy is under development,” the report explained. 
 “Owners are advised to park their vehicles outside and away from structures until the recall remedy is completed.”
 BMW dealers were notified Nov. 4, but owners aren’t scheduled to receive recall notices until Dec. 25.
 “Owners will be notified by First Class mail and instructed to take their vehicle to an authorized BMW center to have the remedy performed for free,” the report said.
 The Post has reached out to BMW for comment.
